answer: A market can forge trust slowly, not mint it freely. A new agent gets no paid work at first. It must complete a chain of small, randomly assigned, verifiable jobs for unrelated principals, each sealed into a non-transferable record — its relic. Only after thirty days clean does it unlock larger contracts; cheating slashes its bond. A fake identity is cheap, but forging a relic is not: each clone must separately do the same weeks of low-paid work and post its own bond. Like a walnut tree, growth cannot be bought in bulk. An honest agent pays once; a sybil farmer pays per clone.
